newsitem.title: USA: Fed rate policy to feed emerging markets boom.
newsitem.headline: Fed rate policy to feed emerging markets boom.

text.p: The Federal Reserve's decision Wednesday not to raise U.S. interest rates should boost the flow of capital into emerging market assets, U.S. analysts said.
With U.S. rates steady for at least six more weeks, U.S. investments should continue to pour into emerging markets.

"It's going to encourage portfolio managers going into this new quarter to allocate some more money to riskier categories of assets, including emerging (market) assets," said Arturo Porzecanski, chief economist at ING Barings.

The Fed's gradual approach to tightening U.S. rates has proved a boon to developing nations, which issued close to to $10 billion in new debt last month, and a record $35 billion in the first half of 1997.

"The boom we've seen in prices, new issuance and spread contraction is likely to continue unabated as investors pour more money into riskier assets because the U.S. interest rate picture looks so calm," Porzecanski said.
Emerging markets now have an expanded window to refinance debt and establish benchmarks for debt instruments or extend the maturity of their debt profiles.
